subject: Renewal aperture: economic readout, SLA ask, and capacity pulse
messages:
From: Ellie Ramos <ellie@prospectum.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, carlos@prospectum.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage readout + renewal window

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the work on the latency fixes last month — we've seen smoother inference in our staging runs. Attached is a quick export from our internal billing showing token consumption across our main product lanes for Apr–May. High level: overall token spend is up ~42% month-over-month due to feature flags we turned on, and the embeddings-heavy pipeline is driving most of the jump.

We're approaching our contract renewal window in mid-June. Before we lock terms, can your team share:
- a short ROI recap tying the recent perf improvements to projected unit costs (esp for embeddings)
- any suggested commit tiers or burst lanes to avoid overage risk while we scale
- an SLA option that covers latency targets for our realtime endpoint (p95 under 150ms) — last week's blips were around 220ms in the eu-west region

Carlos and I would like a 30–45 minute check-in next week to align. Our preferred times are Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Thanks — appreciate the partnership.

Ellie Ramos
Director of ML Ops | Prospectum Inc.
ellie@prospectum.com

Attachment: prospectum_usage_2027Q1-Q2.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie@prospectum.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage readout + renewal window

Ellie — thanks for the export and the note. Quick read and some initial thoughts below; I'll get a short slide deck and proposed amendment over by Monday.

Summary from our side (initial):
- Consumption: 42% MoM increase tracks with the embeddings rollout notes — good signal of adoption, also explains the shift in token mix toward embedding units (higher per-unit cost).
- Unit economics: with modest batching and a small quantized embedding profile we can reduce embedding token cost ~18–22% without impacting recall for the top-3 retrieval cases.
- SLA: we can commit to a p95 <= 150ms in us-west/us-east for your realtime model under a Dedicated pool + regional routing; eu-west is viable with a cross-region fallback to us-east in the short term (we'll provide expected added latency for fallback).

Attachments I'll include Monday:
- latency_summary_may2027.pdf (regional p50/p95, regressions flagged)
- an ROI one-pager showing cost delta with/without commit and with a quantized embedding runtime
- a proposed term amendment (short) with burst lanes and a canary policy

Proposed call slots (30m): Tue 10:00–10:30 PT, Wed 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works for you?

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: (will share Monday)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie@prospectum.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage readout + renewal window

On Fri, May 28, 2027 at 10:03 AM jonas_weber@redwood.com wrote:
> Ellie — thanks for the export and the note. Quick read and some initial thoughts below; I'll get a short slide deck and proposed amendment over by Monday.
> 
> - SLA: we can commit to a p95 <= 150ms in us-west/us-east for your realtime model under a Dedicated pool + regional routing; eu-west is viable with a cross-region fallback to us-east in the short term (we'll provide expected added latency for fallback).

Ellie — adding from CS/ops:
- If you move the embeddings pipeline to a dedicated GPU pool with the quantized profile I recommended in our Q1 pilot, we can enable a soft burst lane (50% additional capacity) that triggers automatically when token throughput exceeds commit by 12% — this avoids hard throttles and keeps latency stable.
- For the eu-west p95 issues: the root cause last week was a regional GPU driver mismatch on one node class (we've patched and set a rolling verification). You should see fewer 200ms+ blips now; we document all incidents in the shared Drive link.
- I'll attach the latency summary and a proposed term amendment with a 6-month auto-review clause (helps you avoid being locked into a too-large commit while you iterate).

Action items for Monday deliverable:
1) Jonas: ROI one-pager + term amendment draft (legal-friendly)
2) Marissa: latency summary + proposed ops appendix (burst policy, escalation contacts)
3) Ben/Karthik: pricing examples for commit tiers and an emergency surge credit option

I'll block Wed 09:00 PT for the call unless you prefer Tue.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: latency_summary_may2027.pdf (PDF, 120KB), proposed_term_amendment_v2.docx (DOCX, 34KB)
From: Ellie Ramos <ellie@prospectum.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: carlos@prospectum.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage readout + renewal window

Thanks Jonas/Marissa — appreciate the clear next steps. Wed 09:00 PT works for us; please send calendar invite. Two quick clarifications before the call:

1) Pricing sensitivity: our procurement team will push back on multi-quarter commits unless we can see a staged ladder with built-in rollback triggers. If your amendment includes the 6-month auto-review and a step-down option tied to usage delta, that will help.

2) Burst lanes: we like the idea of an automatic soft burst but need clarity on how much it costs vs. an emergency credit. Can your pricing examples include both the predictable commit + soft burst model and an emergency surge credit alternative (cost and lead time to enable)?

If you can attach the ROI one-pager and the pricing table to the invite, that'll speed procurement review. See you Wednesday.

Ellie Ramos
Director of ML Ops | Prospectum Inc.
